subs.title: Equation of a Circle and Basic Properties

questions.q: Two circles \(x^2+y^2=6\) and \(x^2+y^2-6x+8=0\) are given. Then the equation of the circle through their points of intersection and the point \((1,1)\) is
The equation of the circle passing through \((1,1)\) and the points of intersection of \(x^2+y^2+13x-3y=0\), \(2x^2+2y^2+4x-7y-25=0\) is
questions.sol: \((x^2+y^2+13x-3y)+\lambda\left(x^2+y^2+2x-\dfrac72y-\dfrac{25}2\right)=0\) at \((1,1)\): \(12-12\lambda=0\), \(\lambda=1\). Adding and doubling gives (b).

questions.q: The centre of the circle passing through the point \((0,1)\) and touching the curve \(y=x^2\) at \((2,4)\) is
questions.sol: Tangent at \((2,4)\): \(4x-y-4=0\). Family: \((x-2)^2+(y-4)^2+\lambda(4x-y-4)=0\); through \((0,1)\): \(13-5\lambda=0\). Centre \(\left(2-2\lambda,4+\dfrac\lambda2\right)\) with \(\lambda=\dfrac{13}5\).

questions.q: \(AB\) is a diameter of a circle and \(C\) is any point on the circumference of the circle. Then
opts: The area of triangle \(ABC\) is maximum when it is isosceles.
The area of triangle \(ABC\) is minimum when it is isosceles.
The perimeter of \(\Delta ABC\) is minimum when it is isosceles.
questions.sol: Area \(=\dfrac12AB\times\) (distance of \(C\) from \(AB\)), greatest when \(C\) is farthest from \(AB\), i.e. on the perpendicular bisector of \(AB\).

questions.q: The locus of the mid point of a chord of the circle \(x^2+y^2=4\), which subtends a right angle at the origin is
questions.sol: The mid point is at distance \(2\cos45^\circ=\sqrt2\) from the centre.

questions.q: If a circle passes through the point \((a,b)\) and cuts the circle \(x^2+y^2=k^2\) orthogonally, then the equation of the locus of its centre is
questions.sol: For \(x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy+c=0\), orthogonality gives \(c=k^2\); through \((a,b)\): \(a^2+b^2+2ga+2fb+k^2=0\). Put \((-g,-f)=(x,y)\).

questions.q: If the two circles \((x-1)^2+(y-3)^2=r^2\) and \(x^2+y^2-8x+2y+8=0\) intersect in two distinct points, then
questions.sol: Second circle: centre \((4,-1)\), radius \(3\); distance between centres \(5\). Need \(|r-3|<5<r+3\).

questions.q: The lines \(2x-3y=5\) and \(3x-4y=7\) are diameters of a circle of area \(154\) square units. Then the equation of this circle is
The centre of a circle passing through the points \((0,0)\), \((1,0)\) and touching the circle \(x^2+y^2=9\) is
questions.sol: Centre \(\left(\dfrac12,k\right)\). The circle passes through the centre of \(x^2+y^2=9\) and touches it internally, so its diameter is \(3\): \(\dfrac14+k^2=\dfrac94\), \(k=\pm\sqrt2\).

questions.q: The locus of the centre of a circle which touches externally the circle \(x^2+y^2-6x-6y+14=0\) and also touches the \(y\)-axis is given by the equation
questions.sol: Given circle: centre \((3,3)\), radius \(2\). For centre \((h,k)\), radius \(h\): \((h-3)^2+(k-3)^2=(h+2)^2\).

questions.q: The circles \(x^2+y^2-10x+16=0\) and \(x^2+y^2=r^2\) intersect each other in distinct points if
questions.sol: First circle: centre \((5,0)\), radius \(3\). Need \(|r-3|<5<r+3\).

questions.q: The angle between a pair of tangents drawn from a point \(P\) to the circle \(x^2+y^2+4x-6y+9\sin^2\alpha+13\cos^2\alpha=0\) is \(2\alpha\). Then the locus of \(P\) is
questions.sol: Radius\(^2=13-9\sin^2\alpha-13\cos^2\alpha=4\sin^2\alpha\). If \(P\) is at distance \(d\) from the centre \((-2,3)\), \(\sin\alpha=\dfrac{2\sin\alpha}d\), so \(d=2\).

questions.q: The number of common tangents to the circles \(x^2+y^2=4\) and \(x^2+y^2-6x-8y=24\) is
questions.sol: Centres \((0,0)\), \((3,4)\); radii \(2\), \(7\); distance \(5=7-2\): internal contact.

questions.q: Let \(A_0A_1A_2A_3A_4A_5\) be a regular hexagon inscribed in a circle of unit radius. Then the product of the lengths of line segments \(A_0A_1\), \(A_0A_2\) and \(A_0A_4\) is
If two distinct chords, drawn from the point \((p,q)\) on the circle \(x^2+y^2=px+qy\) (where \(pq\ne0\)) are bisected by the \(x\)-axis then
questions.sol: If \((h,0)\) is a mid point, the other end \((2h-p,-q)\) is on the circle: \(2h^2-3ph+p^2+q^2=0\). Two distinct \(h\): \(9p^2>8(p^2+q^2)\).

questions.q: The triangle \(PQR\) is inscribed in the circle \(x^2+y^2=25\). If \(Q\) and \(R\) have coordinates \((3,4)\) and \((-4,3)\) respectively, then \(\angle QPR\) is equal to
questions.sol: \(\vec{OQ}\cdot\vec{OR}=0\), so \(QR\) subtends \(90^\circ\) at the centre and half of it at the circumference.

questions.q: If the circles \(x^2+y^2+2x+2ky+6=0\) and \(x^2+y^2+2ky+k=0\) intersect orthogonally then \(k\) is
Let \(AB\) be a chord of the circle \(x^2+y^2=r^2\) subtending right angle at the centre. Then the locus of the centroid of the triangle \(PAB\) as \(P\) moves on the circle is
questions.sol: With \(A=(r,0)\), \(B=(0,r)\), \(P=(r\cos\theta,r\sin\theta)\) the centroid is \(\left(\dfrac r3(1+\cos\theta),\dfrac r3(1+\sin\theta)\right)\): a circle of radius \(\dfrac r3\).

questions.q: Let \(PQ\) and \(RS\) be tangents at the extremities of the diameter \(PR\) of a circle of radius \(r\). If \(PS\) and \(RQ\) intersect at a point \(X\) on the circumference of the circle, then \(2r\) equals
questions.sol: \(\angle PXR=90^\circ\), so \(\angle PRQ+\angle RPS=90^\circ\). \(\tan\angle PRQ=\dfrac{PQ}{2r}\) and \(\tan\angle RPS=\dfrac{RS}{2r}\) have product \(1\).

questions.q: If the tangent at the point \(P\) on the circle \(x^2+y^2+6x+6y=2\) meets the straight line \(5x-2y+6=0\) at a point \(Q\) on the \(y\)-axis, then the length of \(PQ\) is
questions.sol: \(Q=(0,3)\) and \(PQ\) is the length of the tangent from \(Q\): \(\sqrt{0+9+0+18-2}\).

questions.q: If \(a>2b>0\) then the positive value of \(m\) for which \(y=mx-b\sqrt{1+m^2}\) is a common tangent to \(x^2+y^2=b^2\) and \((x-a)^2+y^2=b^2\) is
questions.sol: Distance of \((a,0)\) from the line is \(b\): \(ma-b\sqrt{1+m^2}=b\sqrt{1+m^2}\), so \(m^2a^2=4b^2(1+m^2)\).

questions.q: The centre of circle inscribed in square formed by the lines \(x^2-8x+12=0\) and \(y^2-14y+45=0\)
questions.sol: Sides \(x=2,6\) and \(y=5,9\); the centre of the square is \((4,7)\).

questions.q: If one of the diameters of the circle \(x^2+y^2-2x-6y+6=0\) is a chord to the circle with centre \((2,1)\), then the radius of the circle is
questions.sol: Given circle: centre \((1,3)\), radius \(2\). Distance between centres \(\sqrt5\); \(R^2=2^2+5\).

questions.q: A circle is given by \(x^2+(y-1)^2=1\), another circle \(C\) touches it externally and also the \(x\)-axis, then the locus of its centre is
Tangent to the curve \(y=x^2+6\) at a point \(P(1,7)\) touches the circle \(x^2+y^2+16x+12y+c=0\) at a point \(Q\). Then the coordinates of \(Q\) are
questions.sol: Tangent: \(2x-y+5=0\). \(Q\) is the foot of the perpendicular from the centre \((-8,-6)\): \(\dfrac{x+8}2=\dfrac{y+6}{-1}=-\dfrac{-16+6+5}5=1\).

questions.q: Let \(ABCD\) be a quadrilateral with area \(18\), with side \(AB\) parallel to the side \(CD\) and \(AB=2CD\). Let \(AD\) be perpendicular to \(AB\) and \(CD\). If a circle is drawn inside the quadrilateral \(ABCD\) touching all the sides, then its radius is
Let \(a\) and \(b\) be non-zero real numbers. Then, the equation \((ax^2+by^2+c)(x^2-5xy+6y^2)=0\) represents
opts: four straight lines, when \(c=0\) and \(a,b\) are of the same sign
two straight lines and a circle, when \(a=b\), and \(c\) is of sign opposite to that of \(a\)
two straight lines and a hyperbola, when \(a\) and \(b\) are of the same sign and \(c\) is of sign opposite to that of \(a\)
a circle and an ellipse, when \(a\) and \(b\) are of the same sign and \(c\) is of sign opposite to that of \(a\).
questions.sol: \(x^2-5xy+6y^2=(x-2y)(x-3y)\) is always two lines; \(ax^2+ay^2+c=0\) with \(\dfrac ca<0\) is a circle.

questions.q: Tangents drawn from the point \(P(1,8)\) to the circle \(x^2+y^2-6x-4y-11=0\) touch the circle at the points \(A\) and \(B\). The equation of the circumcircle of the triangle \(PAB\) is
questions.sol: \(\angle PAC=\angle PBC=90^\circ\) (\(C(3,2)\) the centre), so \(PC\) is a diameter: \((x-1)(x-3)+(y-8)(y-2)=0\).

questions.q: The circle passing through the point \((-1,0)\) and touching the \(y\)-axis at \((0,2)\) also passes through the point
questions.sol: Centre \((h,2)\), radius \(|h|\): \((h+1)^2+4=h^2\) gives \(h=-\dfrac52\). The circle meets the \(x\)-axis where \(\left(x+\dfrac52\right)^2=\dfrac94\): \(x=-1,-4\).

questions.q: The locus of the mid-point of the chord of contact of tangents drawn from points lying on the straight line \(4x-5y=20\) to the circle \(x^2+y^2=9\) is
questions.sol: Chord of contact of \((a,b)\): \(ax+by=9\); chord with mid point \((h,k)\): \(hx+ky=h^2+k^2\). So \(a=\dfrac{9h}{h^2+k^2}\), \(b=\dfrac{9k}{h^2+k^2}\), and \(4a-5b=20\).

questions.q: A line \(y=mx+1\) intersects the circle \((x-3)^2+(y+2)^2=25\) at points \(P\) and \(Q\). If the midpoint of the line segment \(PQ\) has \(x\)-coordinate \(-\dfrac35\), then which one of the following options is correct?
questions.sol: Mid point \(\left(-\dfrac35,1-\dfrac{3m}5\right)\); its join to the centre \((3,-2)\) has slope \(\dfrac{m-5}6\), perpendicular to the chord: \(m(m-5)=-6\), \(m=2,3\).

questions.q: Consider a triangle \(\Delta\) whose two sides lie on the \(x\)-axis and the line \(x+y+1=0\). If the orthocenter of \(\Delta\) is \((1,1)\), then the equation of the circle passing through the vertices of the triangle \(\Delta\) is
questions.sol: One vertex is \(A(-1,0)\). The altitude to the \(x\)-axis is \(x=1\), so \(C=(1,-2)\); the altitude from \(B\) (perpendicular to \(AC\)) is \(y=x\), so \(B=(0,0)\). Circle through these three points.

questions.q: The equation of the tangents drawn from the origin to the circle \(x^2+y^2-2rx-2hy+h^2=0\) are
questions.sol: Centre \((r,h)\), radius \(r\): the circle touches \(x=0\). For \(y=mx\): \((mr-h)^2=r^2(1+m^2)\) gives \(m=\dfrac{h^2-r^2}{2rh}\).

questions.q: A straight line through the vertex \(P\) of a triangle \(PQR\) intersects the side \(QR\) at the point \(S\) and the circumcircle of the triangle \(PQR\) at the point \(T\). If \(S\) is not the centre of the circumcircle, then
questions.sol: Intersecting chords: \(PS\cdot ST=QS\cdot SR\). By AM–GM, \(\dfrac1{PS}+\dfrac1{ST}\ge\dfrac2{\sqrt{PS\cdot ST}}=\dfrac2{\sqrt{QS\cdot SR}}\), and \(\sqrt{QS\cdot SR}\le\dfrac{QS+SR}2=\dfrac{QR}2\). Equality in both would make \(S\) the mid point of two chords, i.e. the centre — which is excluded.

questions.q: Circle(s) touching \(x\)-axis at a distance \(3\) from the origin and having an intercept of length \(2\sqrt7\) on \(y\)-axis is (are)
questions.sol: Centre \((\pm3,k)\), radius \(|k|\); \(y\)-intercept \(2\sqrt{k^2-9}=2\sqrt7\) gives \(k=\pm4\): \(x^2+y^2\mp6x\mp8y+9=0\).

questions.q: A circle \(S\) passes through the point \((0,1)\) and is orthogonal to the circles \((x-1)^2+y^2=16\) and \(x^2+y^2=1\). Then

Let \(RS\) be the diameter of the circle \(x^2+y^2=1\), where \(S\) is the point \((1,0)\). Let \(P\) be a variable point (other than \(R\) and \(S\)) on the circle and tangents to the circle at \(S\) and \(P\) meet at the point \(Q\). The normal to the circle at \(P\) intersects a line drawn through \(Q\) parallel to \(RS\) at point \(E\). Then the locus of \(E\) passes through the point(s)
questions.sol: \(P=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)\), \(Q=\left(1,\tan\dfrac\theta2\right)\). \(E\) has \(y=\tan\dfrac\theta2\) and lies on \(y=x\tan\theta\): \(x=\dfrac{1-y^2}2\). Locus \(y^2=1-2x\), satisfied by (a) and (c).

questions.q: Let \(T\) be the line passing through the points \(P(-2,7)\) and \(Q(2,-5)\). Let \(F_1\) be the set of all pairs of circles \((S_1,S_2)\) such that \(T\) is tangent to \(S_1\) at \(P\) and tangent to \(S_2\) at \(Q\), and also such that \(S_1\) and \(S_2\) touch each other at a point, say, \(M\). Let \(E_1\) be the set representing the locus of \(M\) as the pair \((S_1,S_2)\) varies in \(F_1\). Let the set of all straight line segments joining a pair of distinct points of \(E_1\) and passing through the point \(R(1,1)\) be \(F_2\). Let \(E_2\) be the set of the mid-points of the line segments in the set \(F_2\). Then, which of the following statement(s) is (are) TRUE?
opts: The point \(\left(\dfrac45,\dfrac75\right)\) does NOT lie in \(E_2\)
The point \(\left(0,\dfrac32\right)\) does NOT lie in \(E_1\)
questions.sol: The common tangent at \(M\) meets \(T\) at a point equidistant from \(P,M,Q\), so \(\angle PMQ=90^\circ\): \(E_1\) is the circle on \(PQ\) as diameter, \(x^2+(y-1)^2=40\), without \(P\) and \(Q\). \(E_2\) lies on the circle with diameter from \((0,1)\) to \(R\): \(\left(x-\dfrac12\right)^2+(y-1)^2=\dfrac14\). \(\left(\dfrac45,\dfrac75\right)\) is on it, but it is the mid point of the chord through \(R\) and \(P\), which is not allowed. \(\left(\dfrac12,1\right)\) is the centre of this circle, and \(\left(0,\dfrac32\right)\) is not on \(E_1\).

questions.q: Let \(G\) be a circle of radius \(R>0\). Let \(G_1,G_2,\ldots,G_n\) be \(n\) circles of equal radius \(r>0\). Suppose each of the \(n\) circles \(G_1,G_2,\ldots,G_n\) touches the circle \(G\) externally. Also, for \(i=1,2,\ldots,n-1\), the circle \(G_i\) touches \(G_{i+1}\) externally, and \(G_n\) touches \(G_1\) externally. Then, which of the following statements is/are true?
questions.sol: \((R+r)\sin\dfrac\pi n=r\), so \(R=r\left(\text{cosec}\dfrac\pi n-1\right)\). \(n=4\): \(R=(\sqrt2-1)r\) exactly. \(n=5\): \(R\approx0.70r\). \(n=8\): \(R\approx1.61r\). \(n=12\): \(R=\left(\sqrt2(\sqrt3+1)-1\right)r\).

questions.q: Find the equation of the circle which passes through the point \((2,0)\) and whose centre is the limit of the point of intersection of the lines \(3x+5y=1\), \((2+c)x+5c^2y=1\) as \(c\) tends to \(1\).
questions.sol: Eliminating \(y\): \(x(2+c-3c^2)=1-c^2\), so \(x=\dfrac{1+c}{2+3c}\to\dfrac25\) and \(y\to-\dfrac1{25}\). Radius\(^2=\left(2-\dfrac25\right)^2+\dfrac1{625}=\dfrac{1601}{625}\).

questions.q: Let \(A\) be the centre of the circle \(x^2+y^2-2x-4y-20=0\). Suppose that the tangents at the points \(B(1,7)\) and \(D(4,-2)\) on the circle meet at the point \(C\), find the area of the quadrilateral \(ABCD\).
questions.sol: \(A=(1,2)\), radius \(5\). Tangents: \(y=7\) and \(3x-4y-20=0\) meet at \(C(16,7)\), so \(BC=15\). Area \(=2\times\dfrac12\cdot AB\cdot BC=5\times15\).

questions.q: Find the equations of the circles passing through \((-4,3)\) and touching the lines \(x+y=2\) and \(x-y=2\).
questions.sol: The centre lies on a bisector of the lines; for the region containing \((-4,3)\) this is the \(x\)-axis. Centre \((h,0)\): \((h+4)^2+9=\dfrac{(h-2)^2}2\) gives \(h^2+20h+46=0\), \(h=-10\pm\sqrt{54}\). Circle: \(x^2+y^2-2hx-8h-25=0\). (The book key prints the constant as \(55\pm\sqrt{54}\).)

questions.q: Through a fixed point \((h,k)\) secants are drawn to the circle \(x^2+y^2=r^2\). Show that the locus of the middle points of the secants intercepted by the circle is \(x^2+y^2=hx+ky\)
questions.sol: If \(M(x,y)\) is the mid point, \(OM\) is perpendicular to the secant, i.e. to the join of \(M\) and \((h,k)\): \(x(x-h)+y(y-k)=0\).

questions.q: The abscissae of the two points \(A\) and \(B\) are the roots of the equation \(x^2+2ax-b^2=0\) and their ordinates are the roots of the equation \(x^2+2px-q^2=0\). Find the equation of the circle on \(AB\) as diameter.

Lines \(5x+12y-10=0\) and \(5x-12y-40=0\), touch a circle \(C_1\) of diameter \(6\). If the centre of \(C_1\) lies in the first quadrant, find the equation of the circle \(C_2\) which is concentric with \(C_1\) and cuts intercepts of length \(8\) on these lines.
questions.sol: The lines meet at \(\left(5,-\dfrac54\right)\); bisectors \(x=5\) and \(y=-\dfrac54\). Centre \((5,k)\) in the first quadrant: \(\dfrac{|12k+15|}{13}=3\), \(k=2\). For \(C_2\): \(R^2=3^2+4^2=25\).

questions.q: Let a given line \(L_1\) intersect the \(x\) and \(y\) axes at \(P\) and \(Q\) respectively. Let another line \(L_2\), perpendicular to \(L_1\), cut the \(x\) and \(y\) axis at \(R\) and \(S\), respectively. Show that the locus of the point of intersection of the lines \(PS\) and \(QR\) is a circle passing through the origin.
questions.sol: \(L_1\): \(\dfrac xa+\dfrac yb=1\), \(P(a,0)\), \(Q(0,b)\); \(L_2\): \(\dfrac xb-\dfrac ya=\lambda\), \(R(\lambda b,0)\), \(S(0,-\lambda a)\). \(PS\): \(\lambda(x-a)=y\); \(QR\): \(x=\lambda(b-y)\). Eliminating \(\lambda\): \(x(x-a)=y(b-y)\), i.e. \(x^2+y^2-ax-by=0\).

questions.q: The circle \(x^2+y^2-4x-4y+4=0\) is inscribed in a triangle which has two of its sides along the co-ordinate axes. The locus of the circumcentre of the triangle is \(x+y-xy+k\left(x^2+y^2\right)^{\frac12}=0\), find \(k\).
questions.sol: Third side \(\dfrac xa+\dfrac yb=1\) touches the circle (centre \((2,2)\), radius \(2\), on the origin side): \(1-\dfrac2a-\dfrac2b=2\sqrt{\dfrac1{a^2}+\dfrac1{b^2}}\). The circumcentre is \((h,k)=\left(\dfrac a2,\dfrac b2\right)\): \(hk-h-k=\sqrt{h^2+k^2}\). (The book key prints \(k=\pm1\).)

questions.q: Let \(S\equiv x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy+c=0\) be a given circle. Find the locus of the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the origin upon any chord of \(S\) which subtends a right angle at the origin.
questions.sol: If \((h,k)\) is the foot, the chord is \(hx+ky=h^2+k^2\). Homogenising \(S\) with it and putting coefficient of \(x^2\) + coefficient of \(y^2=0\): \(2+\dfrac{2gh+2fk}{h^2+k^2}+\dfrac c{h^2+k^2}=0\).

questions.q: If \((m_i,1/m_i)\), \(i=1,2,3,4\) are four distinct points on a circle, then show that \(m_1m_2m_3m_4=1\)
questions.sol: Substituting \(\left(m,\dfrac1m\right)\) in \(x^2+y^2+2gx+2fy+c=0\): \(m^4+2gm^3+cm^2+2fm+1=0\), whose four roots have product \(1\).

questions.q: A circle touches the line \(y=x\) at a point \(P\) such that \(OP=4\sqrt2\), where \(O\) is the origin. The circle contains the point \((-10,2)\) in its interior and the length of its chord on the line \(x+y=0\) is \(6\sqrt2\). Determine the equation of the circle.
A point \(P\) is given on the circumference of a circle of radius \(r\). Chord \(QR\) is parallel to the tangent at \(P\). Determine the maximum possible area of the triangle \(PQR\).
questions.sol: If \(QR\) is at distance \(x\) from the centre (on the side away from \(P\)), area \(=(r+x)\sqrt{r^2-x^2}\). Derivative zero: \(r^2-x^2=x(r+x)\), \(x=\dfrac r2\). Area \(=\dfrac{3r}2\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt3r}2\) (equilateral triangle).

questions.q: Two circles, each of radius \(5\) units, touch each other at \((1,2)\). If the equation of their common tangent is \(4x+3y=10\), find the equations of the circles.
questions.sol: Centres are \(5\) units from \((1,2)\) along the normal: \((1,2)\pm5\left(\dfrac45,\dfrac35\right)=(5,5),(-3,-1)\).

questions.q: Three circles touch one another externally. The tangent at their points of contact meet at a point whose distance from a point of contact is \(4\). Find the ratio of the product of the radii to the sum of the radii of the circles.
questions.sol: The point is the incentre of the triangle of centres (sides \(r_1+r_2\), \(r_2+r_3\), \(r_3+r_1\)) and \(4\) is its inradius: \(\dfrac\Delta s=\dfrac{\sqrt{(r_1+r_2+r_3)r_1r_2r_3}}{r_1+r_2+r_3}=4\).

questions.q: Let a circle be given by \(2x(x-a)+y(2y-b)=0\), \((a\ne0,b\ne0)\). Find the condition on \(a\) and \(b\) if two chords, each bisected by the \(x\)-axis, can be drawn to the circle from \(\left(a,\dfrac b2\right)\).
questions.sol: If \((h,0)\) is the mid point, the other end \(\left(2h-a,-\dfrac b2\right)\) lies on \(x^2+y^2-ax-\dfrac b2y=0\): \(4h^2-6ah+2a^2+\dfrac{b^2}2=0\). Two distinct \(h\): \(36a^2>16\left(2a^2+\dfrac{b^2}2\right)\).

questions.q: Consider a family of circles passing through two fixed points \(A(3,7)\) and \(B(6,5)\). Show that the chords in which the circle \(x^2+y^2-4x-6y-3=0\) cuts the members of the family are concurrent at a point. Find the coordinates of this point.
questions.sol: Family: \((x-3)(x-6)+(y-7)(y-5)+\lambda(2x+3y-27)=0\). Subtracting the given circle, the common chord is \((-5x-6y+56)+\lambda(2x+3y-27)=0\), always through the intersection of \(5x+6y=56\) and \(2x+3y=27\).

questions.q: Find the coordinates of the point at which the circle \(x^2+y^2-4x-2y=-4\) and \(x^2+y^2-12x-8y=-36\) touch each other. Also find equations of common tangents touching the circles in distinct points.
questions.sol: Centres \((2,1)\), \((6,4)\), radii \(1\), \(4\), distance \(5\): external contact at the point dividing the centres in \(1:4\). The direct common tangents pass through the external division point \(\left(\dfrac23,0\right)\): \(y=m\left(x-\dfrac23\right)\) with \(\left(\dfrac{4m}3-1\right)^2=1+m^2\), \(m=0,\dfrac{24}7\).

questions.q: A circle passes through three points \(A,B\) and \(C\) with the line segment \(AC\) as its diameter. A line passing through \(A\) intersects the chord \(BC\) at a point \(D\) inside the circle. If angles \(DAB\) and \(CAB\) are \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) respectively and the distance between the point \(A\) and the mid point of the line segment \(DC\) is \(d\), prove that the area of the circle is \(\dfrac{\pi d^2\cos^2\alpha}{\cos^2\alpha+\cos^2\beta+2\cos\alpha\cos\beta\cos(\beta-\alpha)}\).
questions.sol: Let \(AC=2r\); \(\angle ABC=90^\circ\), so \(AB=2r\cos\beta\) and \(AD=\dfrac{2r\cos\beta}{\cos\alpha}\). \(d\) is a median of \(\Delta ADC\) with \(\angle DAC=\beta-\alpha\): \(4d^2=AD^2+AC^2+2AD\cdot AC\cos(\beta-\alpha)\). Substituting, \(d^2\cos^2\alpha=r^2\left[\cos^2\beta+\cos^2\alpha+2\cos\alpha\cos\beta\cos(\beta-\alpha)\right]\).

questions.q: Find the interval in which '\(a\)' lies for which the line \(y+x=0\) bisects two chords drawn from the point \(\left(\dfrac{1+\sqrt2a}2,\dfrac{1-\sqrt2a}2\right)\) to the circle \(2x^2+2y^2-(1+\sqrt2a)x-(1-\sqrt2a)y=0\).
questions.sol: Write the point as \((p,q)\); the circle is \(x^2+y^2-px-qy=0\). If \((t,-t)\) is a mid point, the other end \((2t-p,-2t-q)\) lies on the circle: \(4t^2-3(p-q)t+(p^2+q^2)=0\). Two distinct \(t\): \(9(p-q)^2>16(p^2+q^2)\), i.e. \(18a^2>8(1+2a^2)\).

questions.q:
Let \(C\) be any circle with centre \((0,\sqrt2)\). Prove that at the most two rational points can be there on \(C\).
(A rational point is a point both of whose co-ordinates are rational numbers)
questions.sol: If \((x_1,y_1)\), \((x_2,y_2)\) are rational points on \(C\): \(x_1^2+y_1^2-x_2^2-y_2^2=2\sqrt2(y_1-y_2)\). The left side is rational, so \(y_1=y_2\) and then \(x_1=-x_2\). Thus any two rational points of \(C\) are mirror images in the \(y\)-axis; a third one is impossible.

questions.q: Consider a curve \(ax^2+2hxy+by^2=1\) and a point \(P\) not on the curve. A line drawn from the point \(P\) intersects the curve at points \(Q\) and \(R\). If the product \(PQ\cdot PR\) is independent of the slope of the line, then show that the curve is a circle.
questions.sol: With \(P=(x_0,y_0)\) and points \((x_0+\rho\cos\theta,y_0+\rho\sin\theta)\), \(\rho\) satisfies a quadratic whose product of roots is \(\dfrac{ax_0^2+2hx_0y_0+by_0^2-1}{a\cos^2\theta+h\sin2\theta+b\sin^2\theta}\). The denominator \(\dfrac{a+b}2+\dfrac{a-b}2\cos2\theta+h\sin2\theta\) is independent of \(\theta\) only if \(a=b\) and \(h=0\).

questions.q: \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) are two concentric circles, the radius of \(C_2\) being twice that of \(C_1\). From a point \(P\) on \(C_2\), tangents \(PA\) and \(PB\) are drawn to \(C_1\). Prove that the centroid of the triangle \(PAB\) lies on \(C_1\).
questions.sol: Centre \(O\) at the origin, radius of \(C_1=r\), \(P=(2r,0)\). \(\cos\angle POA=\dfrac r{2r}\), so \(A,B=\left(\dfrac r2,\pm\dfrac{\sqrt3r}2\right)\). Centroid \(=\left(\dfrac{2r+\frac r2+\frac r2}3,0\right)=(r,0)\), a point of \(C_1\).

questions.q: Let \(T_1,T_2\) be two tangents drawn from \((-2,0)\) on to the circle \(C:x^2+y^2=1\). Determine the circles touching \(C\) and having \(T_1,T_2\) as their pairs of tangents. Further find the equations of all possible common tangents to these circles, when taken two at a time.
questions.sol: \(T_{1,2}\): \(y=\pm\dfrac{x+2}{\sqrt3}\) (half-angle \(30^\circ\)). A circle with centre \((h,0)\) touching them has radius \(\dfrac{|h+2|}2\); touching \(C\) externally: \(h=4\), \(r=3\) or \(h=-\dfrac43\), \(r=\dfrac13\). Besides \(T_1,T_2\): \(C\) touches these circles at \((\pm1,0)\), giving \(x=\pm1\); the transverse tangents of the two new circles pass through \(\left(-\dfrac45,0\right)\) (dividing the centres in \(1:9\)) with \(\sin\phi=\dfrac{1/3}{8/15}=\dfrac58\).

questions.q: Consider the family of circles \(x^2+y^2=r^2\), \(2<r<5\). If in the first quadrant, the common tangent to a circle of this family and the ellipse \(4x^2+25y^2=100\) meets the coordinate axes at \(A\) and \(B\), then find the equation of the locus of the mid-point of \(AB\).
questions.sol: Tangent to the ellipse: \(y=mx+c\), \(c^2=25m^2+4\); \(A=\left(-\dfrac cm,0\right)\), \(B=(0,c)\). Mid point \((h,k)\): \(c=2k\), \(m=-\dfrac kh\). So \(4k^2=\dfrac{25k^2}{h^2}+4\).

questions.q: Let \(2x^2+y^2-3xy=0\) be the equation of pair of tangents drawn from the origin \(O\) to a circle of radius \(3\) with centre in the first quadrant. If \(A\) is one of the points of contact, find the length of \(OA\).
questions.sol: The tangents are \(y=x\) and \(y=2x\); angle \(\theta\) between them has \(\tan\theta=\dfrac13\). \(OA=3\cot\dfrac\theta2=3\cdot\dfrac{1+\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}=3(\sqrt{10}+3)\).

questions.q: Find the point on \(x^2+2y^2=6\), which is nearest to the line \(x+y=7\).
questions.sol: At the nearest point the tangent is parallel to the line: slope \(-\dfrac x{2y}=-1\), so \(x=2y\) and \(6y^2=6\). The point on the side of the line is \((2,1)\).

questions.q: Tangents are drawn from \(P(6,8)\) to the circle \(x^2+y^2=r^2\). Find the radius of the circle such that the area of the \(\Delta\) formed by tangents and chord of contact is maximum.
questions.sol: With \(L=\sqrt{100-r^2}\) the area is \(\dfrac{rL^3}{r^2+L^2}=\dfrac{r(100-r^2)^{3/2}}{100}\). Derivative zero: \(100-r^2=3r^2\).

questions.q: If \(I_n\) represents area of \(n\)-sided regular polygon inscribed in a unit circle and \(O_n\) the area of the \(n\)-sided regular polygon circumscribing it, prove that \(I_n=\dfrac{O_n}2\left[1+\sqrt{1-\left(\dfrac{2I_n}n\right)^2}\right]\).
questions.sol: \(I_n=\dfrac n2\sin\dfrac{2\pi}n\), \(O_n=n\tan\dfrac\pi n\). RHS \(=\dfrac n2\tan\dfrac\pi n\left(1+\cos\dfrac{2\pi}n\right)=n\tan\dfrac\pi n\cos^2\dfrac\pi n=\dfrac n2\sin\dfrac{2\pi}n\).

questions.q: Find the centre and radius of the circle formed by all the points represented by \(z=x+iy\) satisfying the relation \(\dfrac{|z-\alpha|}{|z-\beta|}=k\) \((k\ne1)\) where \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are constant complex numbers given by \(\alpha=\alpha_1+i\alpha_2\), \(\beta=\beta_1+i\beta_2\)
questions.sol: \(|z-\alpha|^2=k^2|z-\beta|^2\) gives \(|z|^2-\dfrac{z(\bar\alpha-k^2\bar\beta)+\bar z(\alpha-k^2\beta)}{1-k^2}+\dfrac{|\alpha|^2-k^2|\beta|^2}{1-k^2}=0\). Centre \(\dfrac{\alpha-k^2\beta}{1-k^2}\); radius\(^2=\dfrac{|\alpha-k^2\beta|^2-(1-k^2)(|\alpha|^2-k^2|\beta|^2)}{(1-k^2)^2}=\dfrac{k^2|\alpha-\beta|^2}{(1-k^2)^2}\).

questions.q: Find the equation of the circle touches the line \(2x+3y+1=0\) at the point \((1,-1)\) and is orthogonal to the circle which has the line segment having end points \((0,-1)\) and \((-2,3)\) as the diameter.
questions.sol: Family: \((x-1)^2+(y+1)^2+\lambda(2x+3y+1)=0\). Second circle: \(x^2+y^2+2x-2y-3=0\). Orthogonality: \(2(\lambda-1)-(3\lambda+2)=(2+\lambda)-3\), so \(\lambda=-\dfrac32\).

questions.q: Three circles of radii \(3\), \(4\) and \(5\) units touches each other externally and the tangents drawn at the point of contact intersect at \(P\). Find distance between point \(P\) and point of contact.
questions.sol: \(P\) is the incentre of the triangle of centres (sides \(7,8,9\)) and the distance is its inradius: \(\dfrac{\sqrt{12\cdot5\cdot4\cdot3}}{12}\).

questions.q: The line \(x+3y=0\) is a diameter of the circle \(x^2+y^2-6x+2y=0\).
questions.sol: The centre \((3,-1)\) satisfies \(x+3y=0\).

questions.q: If \(A\) and \(B\) are points in the plane such that \(\dfrac{PA}{PB}=k\) (constant) for all \(P\) on a given circle, then the value of \(k\) cannot be equal to .........
questions.sol: For \(k=1\) the locus of \(P\) is the perpendicular bisector of \(AB\) — a line, not a circle.

questions.q: The points of intersection of the line \(4x-3y-10=0\) and the circle \(x^2+y^2-2x+4y-20=0\), are ...............
The lines \(3x-4y+4=0\), and \(6x-8y-7=0\) are tangents to the same circle. The radius of this circle is.........
questions.sol: The parallel tangents are \(\dfrac{4+\frac72}5=\dfrac32\) apart, which is the diameter.

questions.q: From the origin chords are drawn to the circle \((x-1)^2+y^2=1\). The equation of the locus of the midpoints of these chords is .........
questions.sol: If \((h,k)\) is the mid point, \((2h,2k)\) is on the circle: \((2h-1)^2+4k^2=1\).

questions.q: Let \(x^2+y^2-4x-2y-11=0\) be a circle. A pair of tangents from \((4,5)\) with a pair of radii form a quadrilateral of area .............
questions.sol: Radius \(4\); tangent length \(\sqrt{16+25-16-10-11}=2\). Area \(=\) radius \(\times\) tangent length.

questions.q: The equation of the line passing through the points of intersection of the circles \(3x^2+3y^2-2x+12y-9=0\), and \(x^2+y^2+6x+2y-15=0\) is .........
From the point \(A(0,3)\) on the circle \(x^2+4x+(y-3)^2=0\), a chord \(AB\) is drawn and extended to a point \(M\) such that \(AM=2AB\). The equation of the locus of \(M\) is .....
questions.sol: \(B\) is the mid point of \(AM\): with \(M(h,k)\), \(B=\left(\dfrac h2,\dfrac{k+3}2\right)\) lies on the circle: \(h^2+8h+(k-3)^2=0\).

questions.q: The area of the triangle formed by the tangents from the point \((4,3)\) to the circle \(x^2+y^2=9\) and the line joining their points of contact is...........
questions.sol: \(r=3\), tangent length \(L=4\): area \(=\dfrac{rL^3}{r^2+L^2}\).

questions.q: A polygon of nine sides, each of length \(2\), is inscribed in a circle. The radius of the circle is.........
questions.sol: Each side subtends \(\dfrac{2\pi}9\) at the centre: \(2=2R\sin\dfrac\pi9\).

questions.q: If the circle \(C_1:x^2+y^2=16\) intersects another circle \(C_2\) of radius \(5\) in such a manner that the common chord is of maximum length and has a slope equal to \(\dfrac34\), then the co-ordinates of the centre of \(C_2\) are...........
questions.sol: The longest common chord is a diameter of \(C_1\) (length \(8\)), so the centre of \(C_2\) is at distance \(\sqrt{25-16}=3\) from the origin along the perpendicular direction \(\pm\left(\dfrac35,-\dfrac45\right)\).

questions.q: \(ABC\) is an isosceles triangle inscribed in a circle of radius \(r\). If \(AB=AC\) and \(h\) is the altitude from \(A\) to \(BC\) then the triangle \(ABC\) has perimeter \(P=2\left(\sqrt{2hr-h^2}+\sqrt{2hr}\right)\), area \(A=\) ............... Also \(\lim\limits_{h\to0}\dfrac A{P^3}=\) ...............
questions.sol: Half of \(BC\) is \(\sqrt{r^2-(h-r)^2}=\sqrt{2hr-h^2}\). \(\dfrac A{P^3}=\dfrac{h^{3/2}\sqrt{2r-h}}{8h^{3/2}\left(\sqrt{2r-h}+\sqrt{2r}\right)^3}\to\dfrac{\sqrt{2r}}{8(2\sqrt{2r})^3}\).

questions.q: The area of the triangle formed by the positive \(x\)-axis and the normal and the tangent to the circle \(x^2+y^2=4\) at \((1,\sqrt3)\) is ............
questions.sol: Tangent \(x+\sqrt3y=4\) meets the axis at \((4,0)\); the normal passes through the origin. Area \(=\dfrac12\cdot4\cdot\sqrt3\).

questions.q: If a circle passes through the points of intersection of the coordinate axes with the lines \(\lambda x-y+1=0\) and \(x-2y+3=0\), then the value of \(\lambda\) is .........
questions.sol: The four points are concyclic when the products of the intercepts on the two axes are equal: \(\left(-\dfrac1\lambda\right)(-3)=(1)\left(\dfrac32\right)\).

questions.q: The equation of the locus of the mid-points of chords of the circle \(4x^2+4y^2-12x+4y+1=0\) that subtend an angle of \(2\pi/3\) at its centre is ............
questions.sol: Centre \(\left(\dfrac32,-\dfrac12\right)\), radius \(\dfrac32\). The mid points are at distance \(\dfrac32\cos\dfrac\pi3=\dfrac34\) from the centre.

questions.q: A circle is inscribed in an equilateral triangle of side \(a\). The area of any square inscribed in this circle is ........
questions.sol: Inradius \(\dfrac a{2\sqrt3}\); a square inscribed in a circle of radius \(\rho\) has area \(2\rho^2\).

questions.q: Intercept on the line \(y=x\) by the circle \(x^2+y^2-2x=0\) is \(AB\). Equation of the circle with \(AB\) as diameter is .........

For each natural number \(k\), let \(C_k\) denote the circle with radius \(k\) centimeters and centre at the origin. On the circle \(C_k\), a particle moves \(k\) centimeters in the counter clockwise direction. After completing its motion on \(C_k\), the particle moves to \(C_{k+1}\) in the radial direction. The motion of the particle continues in this manner. The particle starts at \((1,0)\). If the particle crosses the positive direction of the \(x\)-axis for the first time on the circle \(C_n\), then \(n=\)..................
questions.sol: On every circle the particle turns through \(1\) radian. It crosses the positive \(x\)-axis when the total angle exceeds \(2\pi\approx6.28\), i.e. during its \(7^{th}\) radian.

questions.q: The chords of contact of the pair of tangents drawn from each point on the line \(2x+y=4\) to the circle \(x^2+y^2=1\) pass through the point ...............
questions.sol: For the point \((t,4-2t)\) the chord of contact is \(tx+(4-2t)y=1\), i.e. \(t(x-2y)+(4y-1)=0\).

questions.q: Two vertices of an equilateral triangle are \((-1,0)\) and \((1,0)\) and its third vertex lies above the \(x\)-axis. The equation of its circumcircle is .......
questions.sol: Third vertex \((0,\sqrt3)\); circumcentre = centroid \(\left(0,\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\right)\), radius \(\dfrac2{\sqrt3}\).

questions.q:
Let the circles \(C_1:x^2+y^2=9\) and \(C_2:(x-3)^2+(y-4)^2=16\), intersect at the points \(X\) and \(Y\). Suppose that another circle \(C_3:(x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=r^2\) satisfies the following conditions:
(i) centre of \(C_3\) is collinear with the centres of \(C_1\) and \(C_2\),
(ii) \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) both lie inside \(C_3\) and
(iii) \(C_3\) touches \(C_1\) at \(M\) and \(C_2\) at \(N\)
Let the line through \(X\) and \(Y\) intersect \(C_3\) at \(Z\) and \(W\) and let a common tangent of \(C_1\) and \(C_3\) be a tangent to the parabola \(x^2=8\alpha y\).
There are some expressions given in the List-I whose values are given in List-II below :
List-IList-II
(I) \(2h+k\)(P) \(6\)
(II) \(\dfrac{\text{length of }ZW}{\text{length of }XY}\)(Q) \(\sqrt6\)
(III) \(\dfrac{\text{Area of }\Delta MZN}{\text{Area of }\Delta ZMW}\)(R) \(5/4\)
(IV) \(\alpha\)(S) \(21/5\)
(T) \(2\sqrt6\)
(U) \(10/3\)
Which of the following is the only correct combination?
questions.sol: \(C_3\) has diameter \(MN=3+5+4=12\): \(M=\left(-\dfrac95,-\dfrac{12}5\right)\), \(N=\left(\dfrac{27}5,\dfrac{36}5\right)\), centre \(\left(\dfrac95,\dfrac{12}5\right)\), so \(2h+k=6\). \(XY\): \(3x+4y=9\), at distance \(\dfrac95\) from \((0,0)\) and \(\dfrac65\) from the centre of \(C_3\): \(XY=\dfrac{24}5\), \(ZW=\dfrac{24\sqrt6}5\), ratio \(\sqrt6\). \(\Delta MZN=\dfrac12\cdot12\cdot\dfrac{12\sqrt6}5\), \(\Delta ZMW=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{24\sqrt6}5\cdot\dfrac{24}5\): ratio \(\dfrac54\). Tangent at \(M\): \(3x+4y+15=0\); in \(x^2=8\alpha y\): \(x^2+6\alpha x+30\alpha=0\) has equal roots when \(\alpha=\dfrac{10}3\). So (I)-(P), (II)-(Q), (III)-(R), (IV)-(U).

(i) centre of \(C_3\) is collinear with the centres of \(C_1\) and \(C_2\),

There are some expressions given in the List-I whose values are given in List-II below :

(IV) \(\alpha\)(S) \(21/5\)

Which of the following is the only incorrect combination?
questions.sol: \(C_3\) has diameter \(MN=3+5+4=12\): \(M=\left(-\dfrac95,-\dfrac{12}5\right)\), \(N=\left(\dfrac{27}5,\dfrac{36}5\right)\), centre \(\left(\dfrac95,\dfrac{12}5\right)\), so \(2h+k=6\). \(XY\): \(3x+4y=9\), at distance \(\dfrac95\) from \((0,0)\) and \(\dfrac65\) from the centre of \(C_3\): \(XY=\dfrac{24}5\), \(ZW=\dfrac{24\sqrt6}5\), ratio \(\sqrt6\). \(\Delta MZN=\dfrac12\cdot12\cdot\dfrac{12\sqrt6}5\), \(\Delta ZMW=\dfrac12\cdot\dfrac{24\sqrt6}5\cdot\dfrac{24}5\): ratio \(\dfrac54\). questions.q:
Let the straight line \(y=2x\) touch a circle with center \((0,\alpha)\), \(\alpha>0\), and radius \(r\) at a point \(A_1\). Let \(B_1\) be the point on the circle such that the line segment \(A_1B_1\) is a diameter of the circle. Let \(\alpha+r=5+\sqrt5\).
Match each entry in List-I to the correct entry in List-II.
List-IList-II
(P) \(\alpha\) equals(1) \((-2,4)\)
(Q) \(r\) equals(2) \(\sqrt5\)
(R) \(A_1\) equals(3) \((-2,6)\)
(S) \(B_1\) equals(4) \(5\)
(5) \((2,4)\)
The correct option is
questions.sol: \(r=\dfrac\alpha{\sqrt5}\), so \(\alpha\left(1+\dfrac1{\sqrt5}\right)=5+\sqrt5\): \(\alpha=5\), \(r=\sqrt5\). \(A_1\) is the foot of the perpendicular from \((0,5)\) to \(y=2x\): \((2,4)\); \(B_1=2(0,5)-(2,4)=(-2,6)\).

questions.q:
Comprehension
A circle \(C\) of radius \(1\) is inscribed in an equilateral triangle \(PQR\). The points of contact of \(C\) with the sides \(PQ,QR,RP\) are \(D,E,F\), respectively. The line \(PQ\) is given by the equation \(\sqrt3x+y-6=0\) and the point \(D\) is \(\left(\dfrac{3\sqrt3}2,\dfrac32\right)\). Further, it is given that the origin and the centre of \(C\) are on the same side of the line \(PQ\).
The equation of circle \(C\) is
questions.sol: The centre is one unit from \(D\) along the normal to \(PQ\), towards the origin: \(\left(\dfrac{3\sqrt3}2,\dfrac32\right)-\left(\dfrac{\sqrt3}2,\dfrac12\right)=(\sqrt3,1)\).

questions.q:
Comprehension
A circle \(C\) of radius \(1\) is inscribed in an equilateral triangle \(PQR\). The points of contact of \(C\) with the sides \(PQ,QR,RP\) are \(D,E,F\), respectively. The line \(PQ\) is given by the equation \(\sqrt3x+y-6=0\) and the point \(D\) is \(\left(\dfrac{3\sqrt3}2,\dfrac32\right)\). Further, it is given that the origin and the centre of \(C\) are on the same side of the line \(PQ\).
Points \(E\) and \(F\) are given by
questions.sol: Centre \((\sqrt3,1)\); \(D\) is in the direction \(30^\circ\) from it. The other contact points are in the directions \(150^\circ\) and \(270^\circ\): \((\sqrt3,1)+\left(-\dfrac{\sqrt3}2,\dfrac12\right)\) and \((\sqrt3,1)+(0,-1)\).

questions.q:
Comprehension
A circle \(C\) of radius \(1\) is inscribed in an equilateral triangle \(PQR\). The points of contact of \(C\) with the sides \(PQ,QR,RP\) are \(D,E,F\), respectively. The line \(PQ\) is given by the equation \(\sqrt3x+y-6=0\) and the point \(D\) is \(\left(\dfrac{3\sqrt3}2,\dfrac32\right)\). Further, it is given that the origin and the centre of \(C\) are on the same side of the line \(PQ\).
Equations of the sides \(QR,RP\) are
questions.sol: The sides are the tangents at \(\left(\dfrac{\sqrt3}2,\dfrac32\right)\) and \((\sqrt3,0)\) to the circle with centre \((\sqrt3,1)\): \(-\dfrac{\sqrt3}2\left(x-\dfrac{\sqrt3}2\right)+\dfrac12\left(y-\dfrac32\right)=0\), i.e. \(y=\sqrt3x\), and \(y=0\).

A tangent \(PT\) is drawn to the circle \(x^2+y^2=4\) at the point \(P(\sqrt3,1)\). A straight line \(L\), perpendicular to \(PT\) is a tangent to the circle \((x-3)^2+y^2=1\).
A possible equation of \(L\) is

Comprehension
A tangent \(PT\) is drawn to the circle \(x^2+y^2=4\) at the point \(P(\sqrt3,1)\). A straight line \(L\), perpendicular to \(PT\) is a tangent to the circle \((x-3)^2+y^2=1\).
A common tangent of the two circles is
questions.sol: Distance of \(x+2\sqrt2y=6\) from \((0,0)\) is \(\dfrac63=2\) and from \((3,0)\) is \(\dfrac33=1\) — equal to the radii. The others fail for at least one circle. (The book misprints option (a) as \(x=2\).)

questions.q:
Comprehension
Let \(S\) be the circle in the \(xy\)-plane defined by the equation \(x^2+y^2=4\).
Let \(E_1E_2\) and \(F_1F_2\) be the chords of \(S\) passing through the point \(P_0(1,1)\) and parallel to the \(x\)-axis and the \(y\)-axis, respectively. Let \(G_1G_2\) be the chord of \(S\) passing through \(P_0\) and having slope \(-1\). Let the tangents to \(S\) at \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) meet at \(E_3\), the tangents to \(S\) at \(F_1\) and \(F_2\) meet at \(F_3\), and the tangents to \(S\) at \(G_1\) and \(G_2\) meet at \(G_3\). Then, the points \(E_3,F_3\) and \(G_3\) lie on the curve
questions.sol: The chord of contact of \((h,k)\) is \(hx+ky=4\). Matching with \(y=1\), \(x=1\), \(x+y=2\): \(E_3=(0,4)\), \(F_3=(4,0)\), \(G_3=(2,2)\) — all on \(x+y=4\) (the polar of \(P_0\)).

questions.q:
Comprehension
Let \(S\) be the circle in the \(xy\)-plane defined by the equation \(x^2+y^2=4\).
Let \(P\) be a point on the circle \(S\) with both coordinates being positive. Let the tangent to \(S\) at \(P\) intersect the coordinate axes at the points \(M\) and \(N\). Then, the mid-point of the line segment \(MN\) must lie on the curve
questions.sol: Tangent at \((2\cos\theta,2\sin\theta)\): \(x\cos\theta+y\sin\theta=2\); mid point \(\left(\dfrac1{\cos\theta},\dfrac1{\sin\theta}\right)\), so \(\dfrac1{x^2}+\dfrac1{y^2}=1\).

Comprehension
Let \(M=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R:x^2+y^2\le r^2\}\), where \(r>0\). Consider the geometric progression \(a_n=\dfrac1{2^{n-1}}\), \(n=1,2,3,\ldots\) . Let \(S_0=0\) and for \(n\ge1\), let \(S_n\) denote the sum of the first \(n\) terms of this progression. For \(n\ge1\), let \(C_n\) denote the circle with center \((S_{n-1},0)\) and radius \(a_n\), and \(D_n\) denote the circle with center \((S_{n-1},S_{n-1})\) and radius \(a_n\).
Consider \(M\) with \(r=\dfrac{1025}{513}\). Let \(k\) be the number of all those circles \(C_n\) that are inside \(M\). Let \(l\) be the maximum possible number of circles among these \(k\) circles such that no two circles intersect. Then
questions.sol: \(S_{n-1}+a_n=2-\dfrac1{2^{n-1}}<2-\dfrac1{513}\) needs \(2^{n-1}<513\): \(n\le10\), \(k=10\). \(C_n\) covers \(\left[2-\dfrac3{2^{n-1}},2-\dfrac1{2^{n-1}}\right]\) on the \(x\)-axis: consecutive circles overlap, alternate ones do not, so \(l=5\).

Let \(S_0=0\) and for \(n\ge1\), let \(S_n\) denote the sum of the first \(n\) terms of this progression. For \(n\ge1\), let \(C_n\) denote the circle with center \((S_{n-1},0)\) and radius \(a_n\), and \(D_n\) denote the circle with center \((S_{n-1},S_{n-1})\) and radius \(a_n\).
Consider \(M\) with \(r=\dfrac{(2^{199}-1)\sqrt2}{2^{198}}\). The number of all those circles \(D_n\) that are inside \(M\) is
questions.sol: Need \(\sqrt2S_{n-1}+a_n<r\): \(\sqrt2\left(2-\dfrac1{2^{n-2}}\right)+\dfrac1{2^{n-1}}<\sqrt2\left(2-\dfrac1{2^{198}}\right)\), i.e. \(2^{n-1}<\left(2-\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\right)2^{198}\), so \(n-1\le198\).

Statement 1 : The tangents are mutually perpendicular.

opts: Statement-1 is True, Statement-2 is True; Statement-2 is a correct explanation of Statement-1
Statement-1 is True, Statement-2 is True; Statement-2 is NOT a correct explanation for Statement-1

questions.sol: The director circle is \(x^2+y^2=2\cdot169\), and \(17^2+7^2=338\).

Consider, \(L_1:2x+3y+p-3=0\), \(L_2:2x+3y+p+3=0\) where \(p\) is a real number, and \(C:x^2+y^2+6x-10y+30=0\)
Statement - 1 : If line \(L_1\) is a chord of circle \(C\), then line \(L_2\) is not always a diameter of circle \(C\).
Statement - 2 : If line \(L_1\) is a diameter of circle \(C\), then line \(L_2\) is not a chord of circle \(C\).
opts: Statement-1 is True, Statement-2 is True; Statement-2 is a correct explanation of Statement-1
Statement-1 is True, Statement-2 is True; Statement-2 is NOT a correct explanation for Statement-1
Statement-1 is True, Statement-2 is False
Statement-1 is False, Statement-2 is True.
questions.sol: \(C\) has radius \(2\) and the lines are \(\dfrac6{\sqrt{13}}<2\) apart. So when \(L_1\) is a diameter, \(L_2\) is still a chord (Statement-2 false); Statement-1 is clearly true.

questions.q: The centres of two circles \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) each of unit radius are at a distance of \(6\) units from each other. Let \(N\) be the mid point of the line segment joining the centres of \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) and \(C\) be a circle touching circles \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) externally. If a common tangent to \(C_1\) and \(C\) passing through \(N\) is also a common tangent to \(C_2\) and \(C\), then the radius of the circle \(C\) is
questions.sol: Centres \((\mp3,0)\), \(N\) the origin, centre of \(C\) at \((0,k)\), radius \(R\): \(9+k^2=(R+1)^2\). The tangent through \(N\) is \(x-2\sqrt2y=0\) (distance \(1\) from \((3,0)\)); its distance from \((0,k)\) is \(\dfrac{2\sqrt2k}3=R\). So \(9+\dfrac{9R^2}8=(R+1)^2\), i.e. \((R-8)^2=0\).

questions.q: The straight line \(2x-3y=1\) divides the circular region \(x^2+y^2\le6\) into two parts. If \(S=\left\{\left(2,\dfrac34\right),\left(\dfrac52,\dfrac34\right),\left(\dfrac14,-\dfrac14\right),\left(\dfrac18,\dfrac14\right)\right\}\), then the number of point(s) in \(S\) lying inside the smaller part is
questions.sol: The smaller part is the side not containing the centre: \(2x-3y-1>0\), with \(x^2+y^2<6\). \(\left(2,\frac34\right)\) and \(\left(\frac14,-\frac14\right)\) satisfy both; \(\left(\frac52,\frac34\right)\) is outside the circle; \(\left(\frac18,\frac14\right)\) is on the origin side.

questions.q: For how many values of \(p\), the circle \(x^2+y^2+2x+4y-p=0\) and the coordinate axes have exactly three common points?
questions.sol: Centre \((-1,-2)\), radius\(^2=5+p\). Either the circle passes through the origin (\(p=0\): points \((0,0),(-2,0),(0,-4)\)) or touches the \(x\)-axis and cuts the \(y\)-axis (\(p=-1\)). Touching the \(y\)-axis (\(p=-4\)) misses the \(x\)-axis.

questions.q: Let \(O\) be the centre of the circle \(x^2+y^2=r^2\), where \(r>\dfrac{\sqrt5}2\). Suppose \(PQ\) is a chord of this circle and the equation of the line passing through \(P\) and \(Q\) is \(2x+4y=5\). If the centre of the circumcircle of the triangle \(OPQ\) lies on the line \(x+2y=4\), then the value of \(r\) is _____
questions.sol: Circles through \(P,Q\): \(x^2+y^2-r^2+\lambda(2x+4y-5)=0\); through \(O\): \(\lambda=-\dfrac{r^2}5\). Centre \(\left(\dfrac{r^2}5,\dfrac{2r^2}5\right)\) on \(x+2y=4\): \(r^2=4\).

questions.q: Let \(ABC\) be the triangle with \(AB=1\), \(AC=3\) and \(\angle BAC=\dfrac\pi2\). If a circle of radius \(r>0\) touches the sides \(AB\), \(AC\) and also touches internally the circumcircle of the triangle \(ABC\), then the value of \(r\) is ______.
questions.sol: \(A(0,0)\), \(B(1,0)\), \(C(0,3)\): circumcentre \(\left(\dfrac12,\dfrac32\right)\), \(R=\dfrac{\sqrt{10}}2\). Centre \((r,r)\): \(\left(r-\dfrac12\right)^2+\left(r-\dfrac32\right)^2=\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{10}}2-r\right)^2\) gives \(r=4-\sqrt{10}\approx0.84\).

questions.q: Let \(C_1\) be the circle of radius \(1\) with center at the origin. Let \(C_2\) be the circle of radius \(r\) with center at the point \(A=(4,1)\), where \(1<r<3\). Two distinct common tangents \(PQ\) and \(ST\) of \(C_1\) and \(C_2\) are drawn. The tangent \(PQ\) touches \(C_1\) at \(P\) and \(C_2\) at \(Q\). The tangent \(ST\) touches \(C_1\) at \(S\) and \(C_2\) at \(T\). Mid points of the line segments \(PQ\) and \(ST\) are joined to form a line which meets the \(x\)-axis at a point \(B\). If \(AB=\sqrt5\), then the value of \(r^2\) is
questions.sol: The mid points of common tangents lie on the radical axis \(8x+2y-18+r^2=0\), so \(B=\left(\dfrac{18-r^2}8,0\right)\). \(AB^2=\left(\dfrac{14+r^2}8\right)^2+1=5\) gives \(r^2=2\).

Consider an obtuse angled triangle \(ABC\) in which the difference between the largest and the smallest angle is \(\dfrac\pi2\) and whose sides are in arithmetic progression. Suppose that the vertices of this triangle lie on a circle of radius \(1\).
Let \(a\) be the area of the triangle \(ABC\). Then the value of \((64a)^2\) is
questions.sol: Angles \(C\), \(B=\dfrac\pi2-2C\), \(A=C+\dfrac\pi2\); sides \(2\sin A,2\sin B,2\sin C\) in A.P.: \(2\cos2C=\cos C+\sin C\), so \(\cos C-\sin C=\dfrac12\) and \(\sin2C=\dfrac34\), \(\cos2C=\dfrac{\sqrt7}4\). \(a=2\sin A\sin B\sin C=\sin2C\cos2C=\dfrac{3\sqrt7}{16}\), so \((64a)^2=(12\sqrt7)^2\).

Question Stem
Consider an obtuse angled triangle \(ABC\) in which the difference between the largest and the smallest angle is \(\dfrac\pi2\) and whose sides are in arithmetic progression. Suppose that the vertices of this triangle lie on a circle of radius \(1\).
Then the inradius of the triangle \(ABC\) is
questions.sol: Angles \(C\), \(B=\dfrac\pi2-2C\), \(A=C+\dfrac\pi2\); sides \(2\sin A,2\sin B,2\sin C\) in A.P.: \(2\cos2C=\cos C+\sin C\), so \(\cos C-\sin C=\dfrac12\) and \(\sin2C=\dfrac34\), \(\cos2C=\dfrac{\sqrt7}4\). Area \(=\sin2C\cos2C=\dfrac{3\sqrt7}{16}\); semi-perimeter \(=\cos C+\sin C+\cos2C=\dfrac32\cdot\dfrac{\sqrt7}2\). Inradius \(=\dfrac14\).
